name: cis-ubuntu-essentials
title: Ubuntu hardening essentials (inspired by CIS L1)
description: High-value Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 server checks inspired by CIS Level 1. Not certified CIS content - a practical essentials subset.

rules.title: sshd denies root login
rules.rationale: Direct root SSH removes attribution and invites brute force on the one account every attacker knows exists.

rules.title: sshd disables password authentication
rules.rationale: Key-only auth ends credential-stuffing and brute-force as a class.

rules.title: sshd forbids empty passwords
rules.rationale: PermitEmptyPasswords yes is an open door.

rules.title: sshd disables X11 forwarding
rules.rationale: X11 forwarding widens the attack surface of every session; servers rarely need it.

rules.title: sshd limits auth tries to 4 or fewer
rules.rationale: Caps per-connection guessing.

rules.title: /etc/ssh/sshd_config is 0600
rules.rationale: World-readable sshd_config leaks policy to local users.

rules.title: /etc/passwd is 0644
rules.rationale: Writable passwd = instant privilege escalation.

rules.title: /etc/passwd owned by root
rules.rationale: Ownership is the first line of tamper defense.

rules.title: /etc/shadow is 0640 or stricter
rules.rationale: Readable shadow hands every password hash to any local user.

rules.title: /etc/shadow owned by root
rules.rationale: Shadow must answer to root alone (group shadow is the Debian norm).

rules.title: /etc/group is 0644 or stricter
rules.rationale: Group membership edits must be root-only.

rules.title: /etc/gshadow is 0640 or stricter
rules.rationale: Group password hashes deserve shadow-grade protection.

rules.title: /etc/sudoers is 0440
rules.rationale: A writable sudoers is root for whoever can write it.

rules.title: No account has an empty password hash
rules.rationale: An empty hash is passwordless login.

rules.title: root is the only UID-0 account
rules.rationale: A second UID-0 account is a backdoor whether or not it was meant as one.

rules.title: PASS_MAX_DAYS is 365 or less
rules.rationale: Unbounded password lifetime defeats rotation policy where passwords are used at all.

rules.title: Default UMASK is 027 or stricter
rules.rationale: Group/world-readable default file creation leaks data quietly. (CIS wants 027; Ubuntu default 022 fails this honestly.)

rules.title: IPv4 forwarding disabled
rules.rationale: A non-router forwarding packets is a pivot waiting to happen.

rules.title: ICMP redirects not sent
rules.rationale: Hosts are not routers; sending redirects aids MITM.

rules.title: ICMP redirects not accepted
rules.rationale: Accepting redirects lets an attacker reroute your traffic.

rules.title: Secure ICMP redirects not accepted
rules.rationale: Even secure redirects trust the LAN too much.

rules.title: Source-routed packets refused
rules.rationale: Source routing bypasses your routing policy.

rules.title: Martian packets logged
rules.rationale: Spoofed-address packets should at least leave a trace.

rules.title: Reverse-path filtering on
rules.rationale: Drops obviously spoofed source addresses.

rules.title: Broadcast ICMP ignored
rules.rationale: Smurf-attack hygiene.

rules.title: TCP SYN cookies enabled
rules.rationale: Keeps the box reachable under SYN flood.

rules.title: IPv6 router advertisements refused (all)
rules.rationale: Rogue RA = instant IPv6 MITM on the LAN.

rules.title: Full ASLR enabled
rules.rationale: ASLR is the cheapest exploit mitigation there is.

rules.title: SUID core dumps disabled
rules.rationale: SUID cores can leak privileged memory to disk.

rules.title: Magic SysRq disabled
rules.rationale: Console-adjacent users should not get kernel debug powers. (Ubuntu ships 176 - honest fail.)

rules.title: /tmp mounted nodev
rules.rationale: Device nodes in /tmp are a classic escalation trick.

rules.title: /tmp mounted nosuid
rules.rationale: SUID binaries in a world-writable directory end badly.

rules.title: /dev/shm mounted noexec
rules.rationale: Executable shared memory is a favorite fileless-malware home.

rules.title: /dev/shm mounted nosuid
rules.rationale: Same logic as /tmp - no privilege elevation from scratch space.

rules.title: telnet server not installed
rules.rationale: Plaintext remote shells belong to 1995.

rules.title: rsh server not installed
rules.rationale: rsh trusts IP addresses as identity.

rules.title: NIS not installed
rules.rationale: NIS predates the concept of authentication.

rules.title: tftp server not installed
rules.rationale: Unauthenticated file transfer, usually forgotten.

rules.title: auditd installed
rules.rationale: Kernel audit trail for the serious box. (Honest fail on most home systems.)

rules.title: cron is running
rules.rationale: Scheduled hygiene (updates, rotation) rides on cron.
